source.head: eed4d6bb61b789b19f60facc79f9e031765fa4c9
source.scope: three exact preimage paths; relevant inherited 5b source is independently rebound to fixed eed

purpose: Make Full setup await the current request's existing read ACL stage, reject an existing mutex without a completion receipt, and propagate every recorded read-stage error.
intentional_behavior_changes: Full read roots nonempty: replace detached same-executable child with a synchronous call to the existing run_read_acl_only implementation at the same phase position.
An existing named mutex returns an anyhow error with actual io::Error raw_os_error 183 instead of Option::None or successful skip. The newly opened non-owner handle is closed.
Recorded read ACL errors now fail initial Full and explicitly non-refresh ReadAclsOnly as well as refresh. The existing detailed log and generic error text are retained.
The Full progress log accurately describes the completed read stage rather than delegation.

preserved.read_acl_operations_masks_sids_and_inher: exact source-region byte equality; FILE_GENERIC_READ|FILE_GENERIC_EXECUTE to the original sandbox group with original OI|CI flags
preserved.rootset: unchanged build_payload_roots, helper/platform roots, canonical-existing behavior, profile/SSH exclusions, write-root removal and deny-read filtering
preserved.existing_shortcuts: missing-root skip and builtin/group RX checks deliberately remain; no full-restricting read-SID proof is inferred
preserved.token_and_access_masks: no token source, token flags, restricting SID, read-cap or four write/delete denial oracle change
preserved.other_stages: deny-read remains before the read stage; original runtime/write/deny-write operations and existing tests are unchanged apart from one truthful progress log
preserved.wire_and_errors: SetupMode, Payload, SetupErrorCode and error-report serialization unchanged; historical HelperReadAclHelperSpawnFailed variant retained
preserved.dependencies_and_targets: no Cargo, BUILD, lock, workflow, environment, feature or target declaration change
preserved.thread_and_handle: production named mutex, default descriptor, noninheritance, guard ReleaseMutex/CloseHandle unchanged; guard is acquired and dropped in the same synchronous setup thread

original_waits_and_compatibility.initial_non_elevated: Command.status has no local timeout; unchanged
original_waits_and_compatibility.refresh: Command.status has no local timeout; unchanged
original_waits_and_compatibility.same_process_identical_payload: existing B64-keyed singleflight/Condvar unchanged; no independent timeout
original_waits_and_compatibility.cross_process_or_different_payload: session-wide fixed mutex is not keyed by read roots; legitimate concurrency may now fail explicitly instead of reporting an unproved success
original_waits_and_compatibility.mutex_existing_without_owner: also rejected; an object retained by another handle does not attest to completion of this request
original_waits_and_compatibility.rollback: none added; earlier provision/ACL effects may already exist when this stage fails

actual_caller_chain: identity::require_logon_sandbox_creds: optional initial setup then mandatory current-roots refresh
setup::{run_setup_exe_payload,run_setup_refresh_payload}: wait existing helper and propagate nonzero
setup_main::win::run_setup: successful mode body precedes initial marker commit
setup_main::win::run_setup_full: synchronously run_read_acl_only for nonempty roots
run_read_acl_only: acquire current mutex ownership, perform unchanged read operations, reject collected errors

new_physical_control.scope: one test thread, actual isolated named Win32 mutex; no subprocess, global environment or production-name mutation
stages: competing acquisition must return OS 183 and explicit not-ready error
retain independent handle then drop owner
released but retained object must still return OS 183 and not-ready error
close last retained handle then actual owner acquisition succeeds
new_physical_control.ownership: existing guard owns only newly created mutex; independent OpenMutexW handle owned by std OwnedHandle; all drops stay in test thread
does_not_prove: read ACL success for actual Full

pending_native_gate.platform: actual Windows native runner with source, toolchain, helper binaries, complete case log and before/after identity bound
pending_native_gate.cargo_scope_note: do not add --lib; the new module belongs to codex-windows-sandbox-setup bin, not library
pending_native_gate.bazel_invocation: reuse original Windows runner/configuration/budgets; this proposal adds no workflow or execution arguments
pending_native_gate.catalog_requirement: actual unfiltered helper catalog must include the new exact name and retain the original helper roster; selected names above are anchors, not an invented complete runtime count
pending_native_gate.qualifying_output: actual new-case body plus complete original helper/library status, skips/retries/cache/early-return retained; wrapper success alone insufficient
remaining_end_to_end_acceptance: initial Full completes the actual requested read stage before marker/credentials
actual ACL query/set errors fail preparation
actual concurrent distinct requests report explicit non-readiness without a success claim

scope_open: No full-restricting token, finite read-root owner, per-session grant lifetime or new SpawnRequest fields.
Builtin/group RX and missing-root shortcuts remain. Completed operations are not a proof that a restricting read SID can read each object.
No protection against path replacement, concurrent ACL writers or per-request root-set drift after return.
No rollback or removal of earlier partial grants/provisioning.
No new cancellation, helper process kill, descendant lifetime, preserve_descendants or Job BREAKAWAY_OK repair.
No production throughput, bounded startup or legitimate cross-process concurrency qualification.
The independent ACL V3/19d2 diagnostic branch and running native jobs are not changed.
archive_note: Preserve proposed Rust source bytes but use .rs.source.txt when registering them as passive qualification evidence. Patch remains .patch. Actual create/GET publication is recorded separately.
